adversarial_audit.resolution: The S6 control uses at most a small coefficient Gram after exact invariant-range extraction.

adversarial_audit.objection: Randomized range extraction can silently miss invariant vectors.
adversarial_audit.resolution: The target rank is exact, the retained/discarded singular gap is recorded, and every basis is checked against all adjacent generators.

adversarial_audit.objection: A finite sparse audit is already an all-n algorithm.

falsifiers_triggered: Dense physical projector construction is not necessary for finite higher-multiplicity dependency audits.
A compact finite coefficient Gram does not imply an efficient all-n basis transform.
The first selected collision-free S6 multiplicity-two sector does not by itself falsify neutrality.

method_contract.coefficient_gram_reduction: All cross-dependency grading defects are computed from the concatenated leaf-basis Gram, never from dense physical frame operators.
method_contract.orientation_range_factorization: ran(E_e)=Inv(V_nu tensor selected irreps) tensor companion spaces.
method_contract.range_extraction: Finite group averaging is applied to m+O(1) random vectors in the selected tensor space and verified against adjacent generators.
method_contract.rank_oracle: The invariant rank is computed exactly from tensor-product multiplicities before randomized range extraction.
method_contract.scope: This removes the finite dense-memory barrier but still enumerates S_n and is not an efficient all-n transform.

proof_obligations.resolution: Exact representation ranks, generator invariance, and dense W3 leaf ranks agree.
The selected S6 multiplicity-two sector has been audited exactly in coefficient Gram space; its result is recorded without extrapolation.
The finite extractor enumerates every group element and stores physical leaf bases.

summary: Built an invariant-range/coefficient-Gram audit that reaches a 5,625-dimensional S6 multiplicity-two physical sector without dense projectors; the exact balance outcome is recorded and broader multiplicity search remains open.
